[patient]: Hi Dr. Lee, 

My stomach has been really off the last couple of weeks. Lots of loose stools and cramping, mostly a few hours after I take my metformin. I haven’t changed what I’m eating that much. It’s getting kind of hard to deal with at work. Should I stop taking it or cut back?

[clinician]: Hello Mr. Ramirez,

Thank you for your message and for letting me know what’s been going on.

Metformin can commonly cause gastrointestinal side effects such as loose stools, cramping, and nausea, especially at higher doses or if there have been any recent changes in how it’s taken. Even if you haven’t changed your diet much, your body can sometimes become more sensitive over time.

Please do not stop your metformin suddenly on your own, because it’s an important part of keeping your blood sugar under control. However, there are a few steps we can try:

1. Make sure you are taking it with food rather than on an empty stomach.
2. If you are currently taking 1000 mg twice a day, you can reduce the evening dose to 500 mg for the next week to see if that improves your symptoms, while continuing the full morning dose.
3. Keep an eye on your blood sugars during this time and send me a few readings at the end of the week (fasting and before dinner, if possible).

If your stomach symptoms are severe (for example, you see blood in the stool, have a fever, or are feeling very weak or dizzy), please call the clinic or seek urgent care rather than waiting.

If things don’t settle down with this adjustment, we can talk about switching to the extended-release version of metformin or adjusting your regimen further.

Best regards,
Dr. Lee
